label: allin_liquidity_secondaries_2026jun
source: All-In Podcast — Liquidity Summit: secondary markets eating the IPO
host: Kelly Rodriguez, Brad Gerstner (Gavin Baker panelist)

results.summary: Secondary markets for late-stage private companies have become a structural, permanent feature of the capital markets ecosystem, now exceeding 2021 peak volumes and competing with IPOs and M&A as primary exit mechanisms.
results.quote: secondary transactions double the 21 peak in terms of secondary transactions
results.evidence: The quote window (turns 161-165) shows no direct address or self-identification linking the speaker to Baker or any named participant; turn alternation is unclear.

results.summary: Companies staying private longer is a structural trend that is net negative for price discovery and governance quality, but secondary markets are a necessary palliative.
results.quote: I don't think there is actually a good reason to stay private longer
results.evidence: Turn 11 contains the quote but no direct address or self-identification identifies the speaker; the surrounding turns do not clarify who is speaking.

results.summary: Long-only mutual funds (Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Capital Research, Wellington, T. Rowe) are at or near their self-imposed private allocation caps (3-7%), creating a massive wave of pent-up demand that will be unleashed when large private companies go public and exit the illiquid bucket.
results.quote: hundreds of billions of dollars of new late stage demand coming back to the market
results.evidence: Turn 106 contains the quote but no direct address or self-identification is present in the surrounding turns to attribute it to Baker or another participant.

results.summary: Arista Networks and Drivetrain (Driveats/Drivets) are high-conviction positions in the AI networking infrastructure supercycle thesis — reinventing networking for disaggregated AI inference workloads.
results.quote: reinvent networking and Arya and driveets are coming at it in a very different way
results.evidence: The quote window (turns 158-162) shows no direct address or self-identification; the speaker in turn 161 is not identified.

results.summary: Zipline is a high-conviction private investment in autonomous drone delivery — a sector that had a false start but now works, with a path to dramatically lower delivery costs and massive consumption uplift.
results.quote: Atreides is also involved in Zipline
results.evidence: Turn 75 ('We we are selling into this') does not match the Atreides/Zipline context; the surrounding turns 72-74 frame a host-style question about exit liquidity, and the quote window does not contain Baker's self-identification.

results.summary: Sierra (Brett Taylor's company) is an attractive private investment in agent-native enterprise software — building Salesforce-equivalent sales, marketing, and customer service agents from the ground up.
results.quote: Sierra Brett Taylor's company agent native
results.evidence: Turn 145 uses first-person framing consistent with a co-panelist sharing a pick; turn 144 references owning 'most of the ones I want to own' in a VC register, and turn 156 later addresses Baker separately ('you've been one of the earliest'), suggesting this speaker is not Baker.

results.summary: Revolut is an attractive private secondary investment — a next-generation neobank with a modern tech stack, 10s of millions of customers, 14 lines of business, expanding from Europe to the US.
results.quote: Revolut share prices in these secondary markets I got kind of curious
results.evidence: Turn 151 uses retail-investor framing ('I owned some Coinbase, I owned some Robin Hood') and personal curiosity language atypical of a fund CIO; turn 150 introduces the name as a tip received 'backstage' from Thomas Leant, suggesting a host or co-guest.

results.summary: Neurobotics (European AI-powered logistics robotics company based in Germany) is a private investment opportunity — quiet, well-funded, $100M revenue, operating outside the high-visibility Silicon Valley ecosystem.
results.quote: Neurobotics in Europe AI powered logistics robotics
results.evidence: Turn 157 names Neurobotics and turn 159 elaborates; turn 156 directly addresses Baker ('you've been one of the earliest... any names'), making the reply in turn 157/159 Baker's.

results.summary: Vast Space is an attractive private investment in commercial space stations, benefiting from SpaceX's falling launch costs.
results.quote: Vast which is building space stations and we think they're going to win
results.evidence: Turn 163 opens with 'Jason, well, I...' indicating the speaker is addressing Jason and is a different person, and the first-person narrative ('we did uh direct on the cap table and SPV for vast') uses VC/angel language consistent with Jason Calacanis as speaker; 'my my at trades' appears to be a mishearing of 'my Atreides' but the surrounding context of the full turn shows Jason speaking before Baker interjects.

results.summary: Venture firms without material exposure to trillion-dollar-plus private companies (SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI) face serious franchise risk and are engaging in undisciplined 'call option' behavior to compensate.
results.quote: venture firms who don't have exposure behave in strange ways franchise risk
results.evidence: Turn 0 is a host intro/voiceover with music cues, clearly not Baker speaking.

results.summary: Current technology valuations (public and private) are fully valued to stretched — not a bubble like 1999/2000, but more analogous to 2021, with risk of 10-20% public market correction translating to 30-40% drawdowns in high-beta names.
results.quote: everything in the world of technology is pretty fully valued
results.evidence: Turn 127 references 'Gav and I have been doing this 25 years,' directly naming Gavin (Baker) as a separate third party, confirming the speaker is not Baker.
